originalTitle: Trump downplays concerns about sailors onboard USS Abraham Lincoln amid record deployment
summary: President said nine months at sea ‘not nearly long enough’ even as families call for attention to mental health crisis
content: Donald Trump has downplayed concerns about US sailors enduring a record-setting deployment of nearly nine months onboard the USS Abraham Lincoln on Friday, saying the deployment was “not nearly long enough” as concerns mount over mental health and supply issues onboard the aircraft carrier. The US president made the comments during a brief exchange with reporters before flying to New York for an event highlighting falling violent crime rates across the US. “That ship is moving right now, or very shortly, and it’s being replaced with another very similar ship,” Trump said when asked about the lengthy deployment. When asked by reporters whether family members were worried about the situation, the president claimed: “No, they’re not.” The Lincoln has been supporting the US war against Iran, and several Democratic lawmakers are pressing the Pentagon for accountability over conditions onboard the carrier. The defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, on Thursday said those conditions had been “completely misrepresented”. Military families and US Congress members have called attention to the intensifying mental health crisis for those onboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, as its 5,000 sailors and marines endure a record-breaking deployment at sea tied to the war with Iran. The scrutiny comes as the navy has reimposed a blockade on Iranian ports in the crucial strait of Hormuz, even as hostilities between the US and Iran have calmed in recent weeks. The Trump administration has offered no clarity on how it intends to wind down the war, while Hegseth has suggested the US military can maintain the blockage of Iranian ports “indefinitely”. Another aircraft carrier, the USS George Washington, left port in Da Nang, Vietnam, last week and is expected to replace the Lincoln, one of two aircraft carriers currently deployed in the Middle East. Two leading specialist military papers, the Navy Times and Stars and Stripes, reported that there have been multiple attempts by sailors to jump overboard as poor conditions and mental stresses on the Lincoln reach a breaking point in its ninth month at sea. One sailor succeeded in early August, a US official confirmed. “The sailor was quickly recovered by an air wing search and rescue helicopter, treated by Abraham Lincoln’s medical department, and transferred off ship for follow-on care.” Worried families expressed their concerns about loved ones onboard the Lincoln at an emotional town hall meeting with navy leaders in San Diego last week, Stars and Stripes reported. One spouse among the 200 or so family members said that her husband had texted her that day saying “he hopes he doesn’t wake up tomorrow”. The US navy said it has “not observed an increase in suicidal ideations or attempts aboard the ship”, but declined to provide data, citing operational security and patient privacy concerns. The Lincoln is “operating in a highly contested environment where traditional supply hubs in the Middle East were disrupted by combat actions”, the US official said, adding that navy leaders had “prioritized mission-critical supplies: first food, then hygiene items, then mail”. “Current reports from the ship confirm continuous access to clean water, functional [air conditioning], and healthy meal options,” the official claimed. In a statement released on Friday, Hung Cao, the acting secretary of the navy, similarly downplayed the reports, saying that “sailors and marines are expected to dig deep” and accused the media of “trying to paint our warriors as victims”. The statement acknowledged that a “small number” of mental health cases were “treated with no loss of life”, and added that “there is no question our young men and women have been pushed to their limits”.
chineseTitle: 特朗普淡化了对亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰部署创纪录的水手的担忧
chineseSummary: 总统表示海上九个月“还不够长”，尽管家人呼吁关注心理健康危机
chineseContent: 周五，唐纳德·特朗普淡化了对美国水手在亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰上经历创纪录的近九个月部署的担忧，称部署时间“还不够长”，因为人们对航母上心理健康和供应问题的担忧日益加剧。美国总统在飞往纽约参加一场强调美国暴力犯罪率下降的活动之前与记者进行了简短的交流，发表了上述言论。当被问及漫长的部署时，特朗普表示：“那艘船正在移动，或者很快就会移动，并且将被另一艘非常相似的船取代。”当记者问其家人是否担心这种情况时，总统声称：“不，他们不担心。”林肯号一直支持美国对伊朗的战争，几名民主党议员正在向五角大楼施压，要求其对航母上的条件承担责任。国防部长皮特·赫格斯周四表示，这些条件“完全被歪曲”。军人家属和美国国会议员呼吁关注亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰上日益严重的心理健康危机，因为该舰上的 5,000 名水手和海军陆战队员正在经历与伊朗战争有关的破纪录的海上部署。尽管美国和伊朗之间的敌对行动最近几周已经平息，但美国海军仍对重要的霍尔木兹海峡的伊朗港口重新实施了封锁。特朗普政府没有明确说明打算如何结束战争，而赫格塞斯则暗示美军可以“无限期”维持对伊朗港口的封锁。另一艘航空母舰乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰上周离开越南岘港港，预计将取代林肯号航空母舰，这是美国两艘航空母舰之一
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
